method: Three candidate central claims per book; labels are hypotheses until source mapping, counterevidence review, and score arithmetic pass.

hypotheses.claim: Reciprocity, commitment, social proof, liking, authority, and scarcity can causally influence compliance.
Influence effects depend on context, culture, motive, and target awareness.
The six principles form a comprehensive and reliably portable taxonomy of persuasion.
Dissonance and self-justification can shift attitudes after choices or harmful acts.
Self-serving reconstruction can escalate commitment and impede apology or correction.
A single dissonance mechanism explains most persistent false belief and institutional error.
Moral judgment draws on both automatic affect and controlled reasoning.
Ingroup cooperation can coexist with intergroup bias and conflict.
Controlled reasoning reliably produces utilitarian judgments fit to serve as a shared global morality.
Kahneman and Tversky established reproducible deviations from expected-utility and Bayesian ideals.
Prospect theory and heuristics research changed economics, medicine, and policy.
The collaborators' personal dynamic is a sufficient causal explanation for the research program's success and rupture.
Situational roles, authority, norms, and institutional design can strongly influence harmful behavior.
The Stanford Prison Experiment validly demonstrated ordinary people spontaneously becoming abusive guards.
Stanford Prison dynamics generalize directly to Abu Ghraib and other real atrocities.
Observers commonly underweight situational causes when explaining others' behavior.
Behavior varies substantially across situations and is best modeled through person-situation interaction.
Broad personality traits contribute little stable predictive value across contexts.
People often overestimate the intensity or duration of future emotional reactions.
Focalism, adaptation, and misconstrual contribute to affective forecasting errors.
These biases make people broadly unable to identify what will improve their happiness.
Close relationships, meaningful activity, and prosocial engagement are robust correlates of well-being.
Adaptation and comparison limit durable happiness gains from many external changes.
Ancient wisdom traditions converge on a scientifically validated formula for flourishing.
Human reasoning often serves the production and evaluation of arguments in social settings.
Diverse groups can outperform isolated reasoners when claims are genuinely contested and evidence is shared.
Argumentation is the primary evolved function explaining confirmation bias and most characteristic reasoning failures.
People systematically overestimate the depth of their mechanistic understanding.
Human knowledge is distributed across people, artifacts, and institutions.
Recognizing collective dependence reliably produces better individual and public decisions.
